variants.behaviorHint: With head lowered, lowers his voice for the first time.

variants.text: Your Honor, I held on to the time I cared for Mother as if it were proof for the inheritance. That feeling enlarged the case.
variants.behaviorHint: Where anger fades, shame rises.

variants.text: Even after learning about the money my brother had hidden, I first looked only at my own grievance. My assumption of entitlement is also my responsibility.
variants.behaviorHint: Folds his hands on his knees and slowly admits it.

variants.text: Rather than seeing Mother as she was, I held on to her as someone who should recognize my effort.
variants.behaviorHint: Starts to say his brother's name, then speaks only to the Judge.

variants.text: I clung harder to the numbers because I feared losing the place of eldest son. Out of fear, I saw my brother only as malicious.
variants.behaviorHint: Breathes as if long-held pride has bent.

variants.text: Before asking what Mother wanted, I calculated my share. That is how I used Mother.
variants.behaviorHint: His ending drops, and his gaze rests on the back of his hand.

variants.text: My brother was not the only one who changed Mother. I also tried to use Mother's heart as evidence for my side.
variants.behaviorHint: His shoulders drop when he speaks of his own responsibility.

variants.text: It is true I cared for her, but it is also true I pushed with the feeling that I should receive more for it.
variants.behaviorHint: His throat tightens, but he finishes the sentence.

variants.text: Your Honor, I put my own hurt and pride ahead of Mother's final wishes.
variants.behaviorHint: Suppresses the habit of making excuses and ends with an admission.

variants.text: I will admit it now. The name of eldest son felt like a right to me, and that feeling clouded my judgment.
variants.behaviorHint: After a long silence, confesses calmly.

entries.questionText: Mr. Yoon Jeong-hoo, even if there was a reason for you to protect your brother, doesn’t that mean you are also responsible for changing the meaning of the ratio that your mother originally wrote down?

variants.text: Saying I tried to avoid the other side finding out does not erase responsibility. At the time, though, I saw no other path.
variants.behaviorHint: Pauses one beat before answering and looks at the edge of the document.

variants.text: I admit I could not leave Mother's wishes as they were. But the reason was not only my own benefit.
variants.behaviorHint: In a low voice, first limits the scope of admission.

variants.text: I do not intend to avoid responsibility for changing it. But I ask that the background of that choice be seen as well.
variants.behaviorHint: Does not avoid the gaze for long, but closes off the ending.

variants.text: Your Honor, I know that the words “for my brother” do not settle everything.
variants.behaviorHint: Answers carefully with his fingers folded together.

variants.text: My hand touched that document. That fact is not erased by saying I tried to avoid the other side finding out.
variants.behaviorHint: Catches his breath, then avoids only the key word.

variants.text: Touching Mother's wishes is serious. I knew that weight and still could not stop at the time.
variants.behaviorHint: His jaw tightens, but his voice stays even.

variants.text: Responsibility does not disappear. I only believed I was avoiding a greater wound.
variants.behaviorHint: Gives a small nod and draws the line again.

variants.text: Saying I tried to avoid the other side finding out is only my motive. It does not erase responsibility for the result.
variants.behaviorHint: Presses his lips, then gives only the necessary facts.

variants.text: I will not insist that choice was right. I now know the flaw in what I did.
variants.behaviorHint: Suppresses emotion and leaves long gaps between sentences.

variants.text: I admit that I am the one who changed the document. Even if there was a reason, the responsibility remains.
variants.behaviorHint: Tries to speak calmly to the end.

entries.questionText: Mr. Yoon Jeong-hoo, even if there was a reason for you to protect your brother, doesn’t that mean you are also responsible for changing the meaning of the ratio that your mother originally wrote down?

variants.text: The responsibility for rewriting the handwritten draft is mine. Saying I tried to avoid the other side finding out cannot be an excuse.
variants.behaviorHint: Chooses his words, then lets out one long breath.

variants.text: I adjusted Mother's wishes. I had the justification of protection, but that justification cannot replace procedure.
variants.behaviorHint: Answers while slowly rubbing the edge of the desk.

variants.text: Your Honor, I lowered the numbers because I feared my brother would collapse. Still, the person who touched Mother's wishes is me.
variants.behaviorHint: Does not avert his eyes when he reaches the key point.

variants.text: I can explain that it was for my brother. But the fact remains that I rewrote the wishes Mother left behind.
variants.behaviorHint: His voice is low, but the admission is clear.

variants.text: I made an unlawful choice in the name of good faith. I will not look at those two things as if they were separate.
variants.behaviorHint: Speaks in short fragments, then lengthens when giving the reason.

variants.text: I believed I was reducing my brother's shock, but I ended up reducing Mother's intent as well.
variants.behaviorHint: Starts to look toward his brother, then looks back at the Judge.

variants.text: I acted as if I had become the protector. But I had no right to change Mother's wishes.
variants.behaviorHint: Keeps emotion down and does not avoid the word responsibility.

variants.text: That responsibility remains even if it was not about money. What is greater is that I judged in someone else's place.
variants.behaviorHint: Pauses at the end of each sentence to adjust the scope.

variants.text: There was a reason to avoid the other side finding out. But that reason cannot stand above the law or Mother's wishes.
variants.behaviorHint: Traces the sequence rather than dates, as if recalling the record.

variants.text: I am not explaining to reduce responsibility. I am saying to the end why that responsibility arose.
variants.behaviorHint: Straightens his posture to hide his wavering.

entries.questionText: Mr. Yoon Jeong-hoo, even if there was a reason for you to protect your brother, doesn’t that mean you are also responsible for changing the meaning of the ratio that your mother originally wrote down?

variants.text: Yes. The reason of avoiding the other side finding out does not erase responsibility for changing the meaning of the ratio Mother first wrote.
variants.behaviorHint: Closes his eyes once, opens them, and confesses quietly.

variants.text: Your Honor, I handled Mother's wishes in my own way to hide a sensitive fact tied to my birth. That responsibility is entirely mine.
variants.behaviorHint: His voice cracks faintly in the final sentence.

variants.text: Saying I tried to protect him cannot cover forgery. I rewrote Mother's final wishes by my own judgment.
variants.behaviorHint: His calm expression does not break, but his breathing lengthens.

variants.text: It is true that I feared my brother would collapse, and it is also true that I changed the document.
variants.behaviorHint: Carries the sentence to the end as if he will hide no more.

variants.text: I touched someone else's wishes in the name of good faith. That good faith does not exempt me.
variants.behaviorHint: Admits responsibility without being able to look toward his brother.

variants.text: I am the one who changed Mother's handwritten draft from 90 for me and 10 for my brother to 60 for me and 40 for him. Even if it was for my brother, it was wrong.
variants.behaviorHint: Takes his hands off the document and looks straight at the Judge.

variants.text: While trying to avoid the other side finding out, I delayed the truth my brother needed and damaged Mother's wishes.
variants.behaviorHint: Continues as if releasing words long held back.

variants.text: Your Honor, I will not avoid responsibility. The choice I made to protect him left wounds both legally and relationally.
variants.behaviorHint: His ending falls low, but the core does not blur.

variants.text: I judged in my brother's place and changed the document in Mother's place. Those two things are my responsibility.
variants.behaviorHint: After a silence, places the heaviest fact on the record.

variants.text: I admit it now. The deeper the reason, the more clearly responsibility remains; it does not disappear.
variants.behaviorHint: With head lowered, puts responsibility before excuses.

entries.questionText: Do you now admit that in the end, both brothers were unable to leave their mother as she was?

variants.text: I cannot say those words are completely wrong. Both my brother and I held Mother's wishes in our own ways.
variants.behaviorHint: Pauses one beat before answering and looks at the edge of the document.

variants.text: I thought I was protecting Mother, but in truth there were parts where I put my own judgment first.
variants.behaviorHint: In a low voice, first limits the scope of admission.

variants.text: My brother read Mother's wishes through his grievance, and I read them through my fear.
variants.behaviorHint: Does not avoid the gaze for long, but closes off the ending.

variants.text: Your Honor, saying that neither of us left Mother as she was is heavy, but hard to avoid.
variants.behaviorHint: Answers carefully with his fingers folded together.

variants.text: I tried to block my brother, and my brother clung to his share. Between us, Mother's wishes were shaken.
variants.behaviorHint: Catches his breath, then avoids only the key word.

variants.text: Even if I take all responsibility alone, my brother's assumption of entitlement does not disappear.
variants.behaviorHint: His jaw tightens, but his voice stays even.

variants.text: My brother had hurt, and I had fear. Both of us looked at Mother through those feelings.
variants.behaviorHint: Gives a small nod and draws the line again.

variants.text: It is still hard to put in one sentence, but no one left Mother's wishes untouched.
variants.behaviorHint: Presses his lips, then gives only the necessary facts.

variants.text: I said I was protecting her, and my brother said he cared for her. Both of us put Mother inside our own words.
variants.behaviorHint: Suppresses emotion and leaves long gaps between sentences.

variants.text: I cannot immediately deny that. I am the one who altered Mother's wishes first.
variants.behaviorHint: Tries to speak calmly to the end.

entries.questionText: Do you now admit that in the end, both brothers were unable to leave their mother as she was?

variants.text: I admit it. My brother twisted Mother's wishes through the heart of eldest son, and I twisted them through the excuse of protection.
variants.behaviorHint: Chooses his words, then lets out one long breath.

variants.text: It was not only my brother who used Mother, and it was not only I who sacrificed. We both held on in our own ways.
variants.behaviorHint: Answers while slowly rubbing the edge of the desk.

variants.text: Your Honor, my brother took his share for granted, and I changed the wishes. Neither side was whole.
variants.behaviorHint: Does not avert his eyes when he reaches the key point.

variants.text: I speak of good faith, but in the result I arranged Mother's wishes with my own hands. My brother also read those wishes through his hurt.
variants.behaviorHint: His voice is low, but the admission is clear.

variants.text: We may both say we loved Mother. But love cannot replace her wishes.
variants.behaviorHint: Speaks in short fragments, then lengthens when giving the reason.

variants.text: My brother saw Mother as proof of his labor, and I used Mother as the reason to protect my brother.
variants.behaviorHint: Starts to look toward his brother, then looks back at the Judge.

variants.text: Mother's remaining heart changed between two people's fear and pride.
variants.behaviorHint: Keeps emotion down and does not avoid the word responsibility.

variants.text: This is why I cannot only blame my brother. I also failed to leave Mother's wishes as they were.
variants.behaviorHint: Pauses at the end of each sentence to adjust the scope.

variants.text: My brother's entitlement and my manipulation led to the same result in different ways.
variants.behaviorHint: Traces the sequence rather than dates, as if recalling the record.

variants.text: I said I was protecting Mother, but in truth I changed her wishes into a form I could bear.
variants.behaviorHint: Straightens his posture to hide his wavering.

entries.questionText: Do you now admit that in the end, both brothers were unable to leave their mother as she was?

variants.text: I admit it. Neither my brother nor I left Mother as she was, and Mother's wishes were distorted twice in our hands.
variants.behaviorHint: Closes his eyes once, opens them, and confesses quietly.

variants.text: Your Honor, my brother read Mother through the right of eldest son, and I changed Mother's wishes under the excuse of protection.
variants.behaviorHint: His voice cracks faintly in the final sentence.

variants.text: We both said we loved Mother, but in the end we placed our own fears on top of her wishes.
variants.behaviorHint: His calm expression does not break, but his breathing lengthens.

variants.text: I changed Mother's first written ratio in the name of protecting my brother, and my brother believed his years of care entitled him to more.
variants.behaviorHint: Carries the sentence to the end as if he will hide no more.

variants.text: This case is not only about who was worse. It is about both of us handling Mother's wishes in our own ways.
variants.behaviorHint: Admits responsibility without being able to look toward his brother.

variants.text: I damaged Mother's wishes legally, and my brother saw those wishes only through the standard of his own hurt.
variants.behaviorHint: Takes his hands off the document and looks straight at the Judge.

variants.text: Your Honor, what I did is clearly wrong, and my brother's heart also failed to see Mother's wishes as they were.
variants.behaviorHint: Continues as if releasing words long held back.

variants.text: Mother's words became both evidence and a shield between us. That is the most painful part.
variants.behaviorHint: His ending falls low, but the core does not blur.

variants.text: I do not want to hide behind blaming my brother. I am also someone who trapped Mother inside the excuse of protection.
variants.behaviorHint: After a silence, places the heaviest fact on the record.

variants.text: I will admit it now. Both of us held on to our own fears before Mother's final wishes.
variants.behaviorHint: With head lowered, puts responsibility before excuses.

variants.text: After the verdict, Yoon Tae-seong had to admit that the eldest-son role he had clung to had kept him from properly hearing Mother's wishes. Yoon Jeong-hu's responsibility for touching the document remained separate, but Tae-seong's claim that everything was void and his quick judgment of his younger brother long obscured the core facts. The property settlement moved into a process of verifying the handwritten draft and the long-running support. Before saying he deserved more, Tae-seong had to explain what he had taken for granted. The brothers' conversation began again not with apology, but with confirming the facts.
variants.behaviorHint: Ending centered on Yoon Tae-seong's responsibility, while Yoon Jeong-hu's document responsibility is not erased.

variants.text: Yoon Tae-seong had pushed the trial with the claim that his younger brother had used their mother, but in the end he had to accept that this claim had begun in his own hurt and pride. Yoon Jeong-hu's involvement in the will remained unlawful, but once it was revealed that he had changed the share and hidden years of support, Tae-seong's attack lost force. In the later settlement, Tae-seong checked again where the money he had believed was Mother's had actually come from, and wrote separately the words and money he owed his brother. Their relationship did not recover at once, but it became clear that anger alone could take them no further.
variants.behaviorHint: Sets Yoon Tae-seong's over-certainty and eldest-son entitlement as the epilogue's axis.

variants.text: The trial did not take Yoon Jeong-hu's manipulation lightly, but it placed greater weight on Yoon Tae-seong's responsibility for treating Mother's final years as proof of his own merit. After saying the inheritance ratio felt like an insult, Tae-seong admitted why he had read his brother's silence as greed so quickly. In the remaining procedure, the validity of the will was separated from settlement of the old account trail, and Tae-seong had to sit down and confirm the substance of the help he had received first. For him, the verdict was less a defeat than a rewriting of his own memory.
variants.behaviorHint: Epilogue where Yoon Tae-seong's interpretive distortion weighs more than legal forgery.

variants.text: For Yoon Tae-seong, the hardest task was not forgiving his brother, but seeing that he had begun the fight after already deciding what Mother's wishes meant. Yoon Jeong-hu did not avoid responsibility for the document, and Tae-seong was told he could not close every issue with that responsibility alone. For the time being, the brothers agreed to limit direct contact and match the property and support records through counsel and a mediator. It was cold, but it was a minimum agreement not to return to the old place where voices only grew louder.
variants.behaviorHint: Emphasizes safe distance and procedural adjustment over emotional recovery.

variants.text: While reading the verdict, Yoon Tae-seong stopped at the line suggesting that his certainty, more than his brother's manipulation, might have trapped Mother for longer. Before asking why Mother had left such a handwritten draft, he had to look back on what answer he had already chosen under the name of eldest son. The procedure for Yoon Jeong-hu's responsibility continued, but Tae-seong also had to correct the part where his claim of nullity erased Mother's remaining intent. In this ending, what the brothers were left with was not victory or defeat, but learning not to use Mother as evidence for themselves.
variants.behaviorHint: Organizes how both brothers distorted Mother's wishes, with Yoon Tae-seong at the center.

variants.text: The verdict placed the greatest weight on Yoon Jeong-hu's responsibility for directly altering the will. Even if the manipulation changed the share and was motivated by protecting his brother, a party altering and submitting Mother's handwritten draft could not be passed over procedurally. Yoon Tae-seong's anger and misunderstanding had reasons behind them, and Jeong-hu agreed to a separate responsibility procedure and property settlement. The secret he had tried to protect remained, but the way he protected it was not justified as well.
variants.behaviorHint: Ending centered on Yoon Jeong-hu's unlawful act.

variants.text: As he left the courtroom, Yoon Jeong-hu accepted for the first time that his silence had not protected his brother, but had taken choices away from him. The handwritten draft, the old account trail, and the context of the old family matter were all taken into account, but the act of altering the document and the concealment that followed remained the central responsibility in the verdict. Yoon Tae-seong had to reconsider the way he had driven his brother into the frame of greed, but at least his challenge to the manipulation itself was found justified. For now, the brothers' relationship had to pass through fulfillment of responsibility before recovery.
variants.behaviorHint: Builds the epilogue by tying Yoon Jeong-hu's silence to his document intervention.

variants.text: The Judge acknowledged that Yoon Jeong-hu's motive was close to good faith, but made clear that good faith did not give him authority to change the numbers in the will. Jeong-hu agreed to preserve the handwritten draft, leave the circumstances of the notarized copy in the official record, and explain the hidden facts to his brother only within the necessary scope. Yoon Tae-seong could not accept the explanation right away, but at least he no longer denied that his brother had not been trying to take more. The time after the verdict began with responsibility documents, not apologies.
variants.behaviorHint: Frames the clash between good intent and illegality with Yoon Jeong-hu's responsibility prevailing.

variants.text: Yoon Jeong-hu's greatest punishment was not only legal responsibility. What remained was the finding that his claim of hiding things because his brother might collapse had in fact made his brother someone who knew nothing. The court ordered a strict reexamination of the effect of the changed will, and advised Jeong-hu to explain the support and the family secret through separate procedures. Yoon Tae-seong was still hurt, but the focus of his anger shifted from his brother's greed to the method his brother had chosen alone.
variants.behaviorHint: Focuses on how Yoon Jeong-hu's protective reason failed.

variants.text: In this conclusion, Yoon Jeong-hu could no longer cover document forgery with the words that he had tried to protect the family. He had known Mother's intent in the handwritten draft, changed the numbers, and decided on his brother's behalf what his brother needed to know. Still, the verdict recorded not only the benefit he sought, but also the catastrophe he had tried to prevent. His responsibility was heavy, but the path left for the brothers was not simple severance. It led to limited disclosure, recalculation, and a delayed explanation.
variants.behaviorHint: Places responsibility on B without erasing the protective context.

variants.text: After the verdict, the brothers could not reconcile immediately. Yoon Jeong-hu had to acknowledge his responsibility for touching the will, and Yoon Tae-seong had to acknowledge his responsibility for reading Mother's wishes through his own standard under the name of eldest son. The handwritten draft, the old account trail, and the old family matter could not be reduced to one sentence, so property settlement and recovery of the relationship were each given time. The only thing that had changed was that, for the first time, the two began fighting on the same facts.
variants.behaviorHint: Most natural joint-responsibility ending.

variants.text: The trial did not set up only one person as the villain. Yoon Jeong-hu rewrote Mother's wishes in the name of protection, and Yoon Tae-seong had already interpreted Mother's wishes in his own favor based on the time he had cared for her. The two accepted that neither had left Mother as she was, though they had done so in different ways. Afterward, the brothers would redo the settlement based on the handwritten draft and the support records, while the scope of disclosure for the old family matter would be decided carefully in a separate procedure.
variants.behaviorHint: Expands the epilogue around Mother's hidden feelings.

variants.text: Yoon Tae-seong had to set down the suspicion that his brother had tried to take more, and Yoon Jeong-hu had to accept that reducing his own share did not erase his responsibility for altering the document. After the verdict, the two reviewed the old account trail from the beginning and wrote down separately what had been believed to be Mother's money and what had in fact been the younger brother's. The work was closer to writing an accurate list of wounds than to reconciliation. Still, they were less likely than before to attack each other over facts they did not know.
variants.behaviorHint: Organizes both the true nature of the money and responsibility for forgery.

variants.text: In the end, the verdict left behind the silence around the numbers longer than the numbers in the will themselves. Tae-seong saw himself assuming that staying beside Mother meant he knew all her wishes, while Jeong-hu saw himself blocking even the facts his brother needed to know in the name of protecting him. The brothers chose not a relationship cut off like an agreed divorce, but a path of remaining a very limited family. They would handle ancestral rites and property matters together, but for the time being would not enter deeply into each other's lives.
variants.behaviorHint: Joint-responsibility ending that includes adjusting distance between the brothers.

variants.text: After the trial, Yoon Tae-seong and Yoon Jeong-hu looked like people who had lost their mother twice: once at the funeral, and again at the place where the Mother's wishes each had believed in collapsed. Jeong-hu's forgery and silence, Tae-seong's certainty and assumption about inheritance, all remained in the record, and neither side remained only a clean victim. The remaining procedure was the division of property, and at the same time the making of a promise not to use Mother's wishes as weapons against each other any longer.
variants.behaviorHint: Includes both emotional epilogue and procedural follow-up.

variants.text: The trial ended without pushing every fact into the public record. The will-handling issue and the ratio in the handwritten draft were recorded within the necessary scope, but the old family matter and details of Mother's diary were placed in a separate private procedure. Before settling property, Yoon Tae-seong and Yoon Jeong-hu entered mediation to decide which truths would be told, and to whom. Protection no longer meant changing a document; it meant setting procedure and the scope of disclosure.
variants.behaviorHint: Ending that protects sensitive family history while simplifying procedure.

variants.text: The conclusion stopped between condemnation and exposure. Yoon Jeong-hu's involvement in the will was acknowledged, and Yoon Tae-seong's misunderstanding was sorted out, but content that could shake the older identity issue would be handled carefully outside the courtroom. The two proceeded with a property agreement based on the handwritten draft and account trail, while the diary contents were disclosed only in limited form to counselors and representatives. It was not an ending that hid again everything Mother had tried to hide, but it was not an ending that burst it all open at once either.
variants.behaviorHint: Emphasizes limited disclosure and mediation procedure.

variants.text: Yoon Tae-seong paused his demand to hear every truth immediately, and Yoon Jeong-hu set down the attitude of deciding alone in the name of protection. After the verdict, the brothers drafted a property agreement and a confidentiality agreement separately. The effect of the will would be reexamined by legal standards, while the old family matter would be handled step by step with party consent and counseling procedures. Because of that cautious pace, the case did not spread into a larger family exposure.
variants.behaviorHint: Protective epilogue based on counseling and a written agreement.

variants.text: The court's final recommendation was simple: correct the wrong in the will, but do not treat the family's most sensitive circumstances like a public punishment. Yoon Jeong-hu took responsibility for the document, and Yoon Tae-seong arranged the procedure on the line of acknowledging his brother's support and Mother's intent in the handwritten draft. The old family matter remained only minimally in the public record, and the brothers promised not to carry its details outside the family. It was not complete reconciliation, but it was an ending that prevented greater destruction.
variants.behaviorHint: Places legal judgment and privacy protection side by side.

variants.text: After the verdict, the two agreed not to sit face to face without counsel. Instead, the mediator divided the handwritten draft, the notarized copy, the account trail, and the diary contents into four tracks and organized the scope of disclosure. The truth Yoon Tae-seong needed would not be hidden, but all details would not be thrown at him before he was ready to bear them. For Yoon Jeong-hu, the procedure was not a convenient shield; it remained as a promise that he would no longer decide alone.
variants.behaviorHint: Establishes procedural protection together with party autonomy.

variants.text: The Judge found that this case could not be ended immediately. The illegality of the will change, Mother's capacity, the effect of the handwritten draft, and the long-running support history each had to be confirmed under different standards. Yoon Jeong-hu's good faith could be considered, but it could not replace document procedure, and Yoon Tae-seong's anger could not turn the capacity issue straight into total invalidity. The two brothers would proceed in order through additional evaluation, mediation, and private counseling.
variants.behaviorHint: Cautious ending that calls for additional procedure.

variants.text: The verdict put procedure before conclusion. The notarization process would be checked again, the handwritten draft and notarized copy would be preserved separately, and the old account trail would be settled without being mixed into inheritance shares. The old family matter was not to be disclosed immediately under the pressure of the inheritance dispute; it was to be handled only after safeguards for the parties were in place. It meant that a family once broken by faulty procedure should not be broken again by another hurried procedure.
variants.behaviorHint: Emphasizes evidence preservation and step-by-step procedure.

variants.text: It was clear that Yoon Jeong-hu had altered the document, but that fact alone could not end all later decisions at once. The Judge separated forgery responsibility, property settlement, and disclosure of the family secret. Yoon Tae-seong was also told to distinguish his claim that his brother was simply greedy from actual loss. The final order was about sequence more than punishment. It warned that the same wound could repeat unless they decided what to confirm first and what to disclose later.
variants.behaviorHint: Epilogue centered on separating procedures.

variants.text: The court held that the more emotionally powerful Mother's diary and the account trail were, the more strictly they had to be handled. To prevent either brother from using those materials as weapons to destroy the other, the scope of access and order of submission were set separately. Responsibility for the will change could not be avoided, but the old family matter and Mother's condition in her final years would not be disclosed without separate protective procedures. This ending chose a safe next step over a satisfying verdict.
variants.behaviorHint: Emphasizes handling sensitive evidence and limiting access.

variants.text: After the trial, the brothers were given not a completed reconciliation but a list of tasks. Confirmation of the will's effect, the forgery responsibility procedure, settlement of support payments, family counseling, and a promise of private access all remained in order. Yoon Tae-seong had to explain why he had been so certain and insistent before asking whether he would receive more, and Yoon Jeong-hu had to speak responsibly about why he had changed the procedure alone. The verdict warned them not to try to end everything at once, but to return to it in order.
variants.behaviorHint: Procedure-focused ending that lists the follow-up tasks.
